Save figure draws the SVG into every format (PNG, TIFF, JPEG, PDF), so a saved figure matches the preview; needed by the Western panel in bourn.image 0.12.0. Setting descriptions say what each setting does, in units.

nodes.name: Scatter plot
nodes.description: Points from two numeric columns, one series per group value.

nodes.name: Bar plot
nodes.description: Group means with error bars, and the raw values as dots.

nodes.name: Compose figure
nodes.description: Arrange charts, images and figures on a page of a set width, in Focus mode. Panels follow their source: rerunning updates them and keeps the layout.

nodes.name: Compress image
nodes.description: Make a small PNG of an image or a figure at a print size, for documents with a size limit: fewer colours (Quality) and optional smoothing (dithering). Save it with Save figure.

nodes.name: Scatter dot plot
nodes.description: Every value as a dot, laid out as a swarm, with a mean or median line.

nodes.name: Box plot
nodes.description: Quartiles, whiskers and outliers per group, with optional notches and means.

nodes.name: Violin plot
nodes.description: Each group's distribution as a mirrored density, with quartile lines.

nodes.name: Histogram
nodes.description: Counts of values in bins, one layer per group; groups share their bins.

nodes.name: Density plot
nodes.description: A smoothed distribution (Gaussian kernel density) per group.

nodes.name: XY line
nodes.description: Mean ± error at each x, joined by a line, one line per group. Optionally a second curve drawn as a line on the same axes (Overlay: such as FRAP fit's fitted curve over FRAP normalize's whole curve), and a dashed vertical line at one x (Mark at x: such as 0, the bleach).

nodes.name: Edit figure
nodes.description: Click elements to restyle them. Formatting only: no value can change here.

nodes.name: Joint plot
nodes.description: A scatter with each variable's histogram along its edge.

nodes.name: Pair plot
nodes.description: Every pair of variables as a scatter, with each one's distribution on the diagonal.

nodes.name: Radar chart
nodes.description: Each group's values across several measures, as an area on spokes.

nodes.name: Angle distribution
nodes.description: A rose diagram: how many angles fall in each sector.

nodes.name: Read figure
nodes.description: Read a finished figure file (SVG, PNG, TIFF, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or JPEG 2000) to compose, compress or save. An SVG stays vector; a raster records whether the file is lossless or lossy. Use Read image for pixels to analyse.

nodes.name: Render figure
nodes.description: Render a figure at its physical size: SVG or PDF (vector), or PNG, TIFF or JPEG at a DPI recorded in the file. JPEG is lossy: for slides, not publication.

nodes.name: Save figure
nodes.description: Write a figure to a file. A chart wired in directly, or an SVG figure (Western panel's, or one Read figure read), is rendered in the format of the file's extension (SVG, PNG, TIFF, JPEG or PDF) at the DPI below; any other rendered figure, including a WebP, AVIF or JPEG 2000 read by Read figure, is written as it was, under its own extension.

nodes.name: Curve fit
nodes.description: Data with a fitted line or model curve and its confidence band.

nodes.name: Survival curve
nodes.description: Kaplan–Meier survival steps per group, with censor marks and a log-rank p.

nodes.name: Volcano plot
nodes.description: Effect against −log10 p, with thresholds and the top hits named.

nodes.name: Heatmap
nodes.description: A table of values as colours, optionally scaled and clustered.

nodes.name: Bland–Altman plot
nodes.description: Agreement of two paired measurements: difference against mean, with bias and limits.

nodes.name: Style designer
nodes.description: Design a style template on sample data, or restyle a connected figure.

nodes.name: Interaction plot
nodes.description: The cell means of a Two-way ANOVA, one series per level of one factor, with the model's interval.

nodes.name: Estimate plot
nodes.description: Each comparison's estimate (or ratio) with its confidence interval, against a reference line.

The former `bourn-align` sample plugin, renamed and grown into Bourn's sequence plugin. It is a clean break: workflows
saved with `bourn-align`'s nodes (`align.read`, `align.kalign`, `align.save`) are not migrated; their nodes are now
`sequence.read`, `sequence.align` and `sequence.save`. The Sequence viewer (`plot.alignment`) keeps its id.

- Read sequences reads a plain text file (a Sanger read) as one sequence named after the file; one sequence per line
  is the explicit format "lines".
- Sequence sets may carry a type per row; Align refuses a set of mixed types, and a name with two sequences, naming them.
- New: Sequences (a typed or pasted reference library and collector) and Sequence selection (the wanted stretch of a
  read, matched against the references by bourn_sequence_native).
- Sequence selection writes its proposal and every candidate (identity, coverage, rank, which was proposed) to its outputs
  (`Match`, `Candidates`), so review shows what the node proposed and the run record says why a reference was picked.
- A held review choice that no longer matches the read, the references or the Output (or is off the codons of its frame
  when the output is protein) refuses the item in words; it is never replaced by the proposal. When no reference is clearly
  ahead the best match's stretch is proposed, with the reference left unpicked.
- Read sequences types each record by its letters: a file mixing DNA and protein is a mixed set with a type per row.

bourn.sheets.name: bourn.sheets
bourn.sheets.description: Open, edit and share spreadsheets in Bourn, and read a sheet into a workflow.

versions.notes:
Bourn Sheets, a spreadsheet tool on the Tools tab (D227). A workbook is a Bourn record: readable JSON is what is kept,
with every saved version listed.

- A grid (IronCalc) with formulas, number formats, merges and frozen panes; English and Traditional Chinese.
- Import an `.xlsx` or a `.csv` (UTF-8, or UTF-16 with its mark); what a workbook cannot keep is listed on import.
  Export `.xlsx`, or one sheet as `.csv` (UTF-8 with a mark, values only).
- One person edits a workbook at a time; others see it read-only with the editor's name.
- The Read sheet node reads a range of one saved version of a workbook into a table.
- A workbook is at most 8 MB.

nodes.name: Read sheet
nodes.description: Read a sheet, a range or a named range of a workbook in Sheets as a table of its computed values. It always reads the saved version you chose, so a later edit never changes a finished run.
